races.title: State House, District 1
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Edward C. Goodwin
cands.bio: Republican state House member for District 1 since 2019. Born in Edenton, he is a farmer and Air Force veteran who served 23 years as a Naval Criminal Investigative Service special agent. He was a Chowan County commissioner from 2008 to 2012 and ran for Secretary of State in 2012.
cands.gaps: We could not find any documented statements or actions by Goodwin on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, campaign-money pledges, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school choice and teacher pay. The Ballotpedia page lists no endorsements for 2024 or 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. The list of bills he sponsored did not load, so we could not review his legislation. His tax and healthcare positions come only from his 2012 statewide campaign and may not reflect his current views.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says he was born in Edenton and grew up on his family's farm, returned to his hometown in 2004 after a federal career, and now lives on the family farm in Edenton.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since 2019 (seven years). Chowan County commissioner 2008-2012. 23-year NCIS special agent and INF Treaty inspector. Air Force veteran with a criminal justice degree. Farmer.
qual.why: Several terms in the legislature and a prior local elected office put him in the high range. His investigative career is only loosely tied to law or policy work. Committee chair and vice-chair posts were not counted.
qual.label: Several terms in the legislature and a prior local elected office put him in the high range. His investigative career is only loosely tied to law or policy work. Committee chair and vice-chair posts were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2012 campaign for Secretary of State, Ballotpedia reports he was pro-life. No details on exceptions or specific policies were given, and the statement is from 2012.

cands.name: Miriam Rollin
cands.bio: Retired attorney and child-advocacy policy leader with a 40-year career. She spent 16 years with Fight Crime: Invest in Kids, prosecuted child abuse and family violence cases, and ran a national education civil rights alliance. Democratic candidate for NC House District 1 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as endorsed by two Sway voter-guide groups, Fair Map Fight Club and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Rollin was born or raised, or the year she moved to North Carolina. She has held no elected office, so there is no legislative record to review. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, policing and pay for officers, gun laws, or abortion. Her campaign site mentions an Albemarle Observer article about a speech in Roper, but we could not read it. Her education and career details come from her own campaign materials and Ballotpedia's survey of her, and we found no independent reporting confirming them.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney with a 40-year career in child and family policy: lobbying Congress and state legislatures, prosecuting child abuse and family violence cases, serving as a civil attorney for neglected children, and leading national coalitions. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: A long law and policy career, including work with legislatures, fits a middle-to-high score. She has no prior legislative service, and her appointed Board of Adjustment seat adds nothing to the score.
